module_title: Major Corridors, Superlatives, and the Golden Quadrilateral
introduction: At this level, we memorize the mega-highway projects that act as the economic arteries of India. We will focus on the Golden Quadrilateral, the intersection of major corridors, and the absolute superlatives (longest and shortest highways).

core_concepts.title: The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ)
core_concepts.description: Launched in 1999, it is a massive highway network connecting India's four top metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. The total length of the GQ is 5,846 kilometers, forming a quadrilateral shape on the map.

core_concepts.title: North-South and East-West Corridors
core_concepts.description: These are two massive cross-country routes. The North-South corridor connects Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). The East-West corridor connects Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat).

core_concepts.title: The Grand Intersection
core_concepts.description: The North-South and East-West corridors physically cross each other at exactly one point in India. This intersection point is 'Jhansi' in Uttar Pradesh.

core_concepts.title: State with Longest Network
core_concepts.description: 'Maharashtra' has the highest total length of National Highways as well as the highest total road network length in India, followed by Uttar Pradesh.

important_entities.name: NH-44
important_entities.significance: Previously known as NH-7, NH-44 runs from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south, covering over 3,745 km and passing through more than 10 states. It represents the entirety of the North-South Corridor.

important_entities.name: NH-118 and NH-548 / NH-966B
important_entities.significance: Historically, exams asked for NH-47A (now renamed NH-966B, connecting Willingdon Island to Kochi, 6 km). Under the new numbering system, NH-118 (Jharkhand) and NH-548 (Maharashtra) are considered the shortest, both being just about 5 km long.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Older textbooks and previous year questions often list 'NH-7' as the longest highway (Varanasi to Kanyakumari). Do not choose NH-7 if NH-44 is in the options. NH-44 is the modern, merged route that includes the old NH-7.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata. The four pillars of India's metropolitan transport.

exam_strategy_tips: The intersection point of the N-S and E-W corridors ('Jhansi') is one of the most frequently asked geography questions in SSC and State PCS exams.
Remember that the Golden Quadrilateral project was initiated under the Prime Ministership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
